tasks.subject: [hosted-notification-intake-bounds] [P1] Add the tenant event-capacity schema and backfill
tasks.description:
Add fixed internal policy constants for a 600-per-UTC-minute tenant arrival budget, 100 active subscriptions per physical binding, 100,000 retained rows, 256 MiB of stored protected payload, 60-second generic storage retry, 100-row cleanup pages, 100 cleanup pages per run, and a 20-second run ceiling. Add `managed_connector_event_capacity` with one cascade-owned row created in the same transaction as every connector tenant; fields for UTC rate window/count, retained rows, protected payload bytes, next cleanup, last cleanup, and updated time; non-negative checks; and a due-cleanup index. Add an append-only Drizzle migration and snapshot. Backfill row count, actual UTF-8 bytes of each non-empty stored protected payload, and earliest capacity-changing expiry. Start rate count at zero. Ingress must never lazily create or repair the ledger. Abort migration on an existing over-limit tenant rather than truncating/deleting data. Add a controlled cutover reconciler: managed-event readiness remains off, old receiver versions are excluded/quiesced, exact inbox aggregates are recomputed under tenant locks, and missing/stale/over-limit ledgers refuse readiness. Simulate an old-version post-backfill write and prove it is caught; no mixed-version zero-downtime accounting is required. Export the table through the existing schema barrel.

Acceptance: all historical migrations stay byte-identical; the migrated offline Postgres fixture proves exact backfill, constraints, index, tenant cascade, and over-limit refusal; schema/type/lint checks pass. Test purpose comments must state which resource invariant can fail.

tasks.subject: [hosted-notification-intake-bounds] [P1] Enforce one lock order and bounded subscription fan-out
tasks.description:
Create a private managed-event capacity service that locks one required tenant ledger using the production Postgres transaction client. Define and document the only lock order: capacity row first, then binding/subscription/inbox rows. Update managed subscription claim to reserve one of 100 non-revoked slots before provider mutation for the same physical binding using the existing authority-command rejection shape. A terminal failed/cancelled/superseded activation releases its reservation and, after any provider trigger mutation, records captured-binding external cleanup through the existing cleanup/recovery contract. Shared triggers remain; an unshared exact trigger is removed. A revoked subscription releases a fan-out slot; it does not delete prior inbox receipts. Ingress must also detect more than 100 historical active subscribers and refuse the whole event rather than partially delivering a first page.

Acceptance: exact boundary 100 succeeds and 101 fails; concurrent activation cannot exceed 100; retry succeeds after revocation; a foreign tenant is independent; a lock-removal mutant makes the concurrency assertion fail; no public owner setting or environment override is added.
tasks.activeForm: Enforcing the event lock order and subscription fan-out bound

tasks.subject: [hosted-notification-intake-bounds] [P2] Admit signed events atomically before charging capacity
tasks.description:
Refactor managed webhook admission so raw size and project signature verification remain before tenant lookup or capacity mutation. Resolve a candidate tenant without mutation, then lock its capacity row and recheck the exact ready binding, provider/account generation, and active subscriptions. Determine existing per-subscription receipt identities before normalization and quota charging. Do not create/reset/update the ledger for an authority refusal or exact duplicate. After the capacity lock and duplicate/refusal decisions, sample `clock_timestamp()` and use its nondecreasing UTC minute for both the effective novel-event window and Retry-After. Preflight the effective novel-event and row ceilings before encryption, then check exact stored bytes. An all-existing redelivery returns accepted without changing ciphertext, deadlines, rate, row, or byte counters. A partial redelivery reserves only missing rows/bytes and one arrival unit. Normalize once, protect each missing payload with exact AAD, measure actual stored UTF-8 bytes, and reject when prospective arrival/row/byte totals exceed a fixed limit. Insert the complete fan-out and update counters in the same transaction, using returned inserts as the final invariant.

Extend the route with one privacy-safe overload contract: HTTP 429, body `{"error":"event_intake_limited"}`, and positive integer `Retry-After`. Rate overload reports seconds to the next database UTC-minute boundary; fan-out/storage report 60 seconds. Do not reveal the private reason, tenant, limit, usage, account, subscription, or payload. Existing 413/415/401/403/503 contracts remain.

Acceptance: exact-at-limit and first-over-limit tests for rate/rows/bytes, complete fan-out, exact and partial duplicate tests, no-state malformed/unauthorized/rejected tests, two-connection concurrency that cannot exceed capacity, a queued minute-rollover control that cannot reset the window backwards, and mounted signed-route response/privacy assertions all pass. Set transaction-local lock timeout to one second and statement timeout to five seconds; map admission lock contention to the generic 429 with Retry-After 1. A capacity-lock mutant and a charge-before-dedupe mutant fail meaningful tests. Production Neon Pool/PGlite proof covers emitted SQL/transactions only; deterministic two-transaction interleaving kills the lock mutant, and the report must not claim PGlite proves lock contention.
tasks.activeForm: Making signed event admission and quota charging atomic

tasks.phaseName: P3 — Capacity release and fair cleanup
tasks.subject: [hosted-notification-intake-bounds] [P3] Release event capacity transactionally and fairly
tasks.description:
Update ACK, seven-day content clearing, 30-day metadata deletion, and tenant deletion behavior to keep the capacity ledger exact. Lock capacity before inbox rows. The first valid ACK or content clear subtracts actual non-empty protected bytes once; repeated ACK/cleanup cannot decrement again. Metadata deletion subtracts one retained row and any remaining bytes. Revocation and disconnection continue to stop new intake without erasing accepted receipts.

Replace global oldest-row cleanup with bounded tenant pages. Select due capacity rows by `last_cleanup_at NULLS FIRST`, `next_cleanup_at`, and tenant id using `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`. Each tenant page uses a fixed small number of set-based statements for at most 100 content clears plus 100 metadata deletes; per-row SQL loops are forbidden. At cleanup-handler entry create one 25-second event-maintenance signal and give retention a 20-second deadline. Before every awaited SQL boundary, check abort/deadline and bound the next statement timeout to the smaller of two seconds and the remaining budget; lock timeout remains one second. Await statement settlement or transaction rollback—never return through an uncancelled `Promise.race`. An already-running query may exceed the scheduling deadline by at most its remaining statement timeout plus bounded driver settlement/rollback. Interrupted pages roll back; result counts include only earlier committed pages. Repeat for at most 100 pages, then pass the same remaining signal to physical-trigger cleanup. Existing account cleanup remains outside the event-maintenance timing claim. A processed tenant moves behind other due tenants but may consume more pages when alone. Concurrent workers skip claimed tenants.

Place opportunistic cleanup after zero-mutation decisions. Signed ingress runs at most one exact-tenant page only after a novel/partial event commits accepted; duplicates, rejected, malformed, and limited outcomes do not clean. Authenticated pull runs at most one exact-tenant page only after principal and input validation, before reading the page. Change the authenticated Vercel cleanup schedule from daily to hourly.

Acceptance: idempotent ACK, all-state expiry, rollback, concurrent ACK/cleanup, exact counter-to-inbox reconciliation, noisy-tenant fairness, concurrent worker, page, duration, and abort tests pass. A deterministic clock/query seam makes multiple individually sub-two-second statements cross a small deadline; the active page rolls back, prior committed counts stay exact, and removing per-SQL checks fails. Duplicate and rejected requests with unrelated expired rows prove zero opportunistic mutation. A selection-order mutant starves a later tenant and fails. Cleanup logs/results contain aggregate counts only.
tasks.activeForm: Releasing event capacity through fair bounded cleanup

Run the focused managed event, schema, cleanup route, transaction client, site typecheck/lint/build, migration, and coverage guards appropriate to changed paths. Preserve exact before/after migration manifests and test at least one restored negative-control mutant for admission, duplicate charging, capacity release, and fairness.

Update `contributing/managed-connections-operations.md` with static limits, generic 429/Retry-After behavior, hourly cleanup, counter/recovery inspection, and the facts that sender retry timing is external, 600/minute bounds novel accepted work rather than total request work, 100,000 rows averages about 3,333 receipt rows/day over 30 days, fan-out multiplies rows, ACK releases bytes only, and row exhaustion may persist until metadata retention. Freeze an exact source/fixture evidence handoff for the DOR-1905 owner to update `contributing/connections-security-verification.md` later; do not depend on that unmerged guide or close unrelated live-pending gates. Do not claim a live provider event or run a live load test. Regenerate site source/API artifacts only if their inputs change.
